title: Importing FDA Pre-Market Approval Logic to AI Safety: A Technical Feasibility Study

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible with gap: the pharmaceutical analogy is frequently invoked but a gap analysis alone does not change governance; impact requires policy adoption of the findings.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: mapping FDA requirements to AI analogs requires understanding both regulatory domains, manageable with guidance but requires cross-domain learning.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Sustained effort: systematically mapping each FDA PMA requirement to an AI analog and assessing feasibility requires thorough analysis across multiple requirement categories.

novelty.reasoning: The FDA-AI regulation analogy has been analyzed by AI Now Institute, Harvard researchers, and NTIA. However, existing work focuses on high-level feasibility arguments rather than a detailed technical requirement-by-requirement mapping of FDA PMA procedures to AI analogs. The systematic mapping approach adds some novelty over existing policy analyses.

evidence: AI Now Institute 'What Can We Learn From the FDA Model for AI Regulation?' provides extensive analysis of FDA analogy feasibility including challenges at foundation model layer
Carpenter et al. (Harvard) 'An FDA for AI? Pitfalls and Plausibility of Approval Regulation for Frontier AI' directly examines pre-market approval feasibility
NTIA AI Accountability Report examines FDA-style food/drug regulation lessons for AI
Multiple analyses identify the 'gate-to-market-entry' problem: FDA power derives from controlling market access, which has no clear AI analog
